dedupe_keys.name: prediction of long range infrasound propagation from tornadoes based on new atmospheric boundary layer wind tunnel experiments

description: Prediction of Long-Range Infrasound Propagation from Tornadoes Based on New Atmospheric Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel Experiments is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "experimental", published or maintained by Tianshu Zhang, University of Florida (ufl.edu). The University of Florida (UF) is developing a fast prediction model for infrasound propagation through turbulence for the purposes of predicting tornado formation, tracking tornadoes, and increasing safety via improved early warning. Tornadoes create low frequency acoustic waves below the threshold of human hearing called infrasound. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "experimental" project. Keywords: Tornado prediction, Infrasaound Propagation, Turbulent-Acoustic Interaction, Wind Tunnel, Acoustic Propagation. Published 2021-06-07. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
